Modelling of red sea urchins, red turban snails, and their ratio in Barkley Sound

Loading in the data and other setup

For using the data I have downloaded clean data from my preliminary explorations that contains all of the exlanantory and response variables that I would like to use. I have also made a separate dataset where I have averaged the values for urchin, snail counts etc. for transects occurring at the same sites. I have also made a theme for all subsequent figures

## Rows: 35 Columns: 27
## ── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Delimiter: ","
## chr   (6): site_code, site_name, region1, region2, region3, region4
## dbl  (19): latitude, longitude, depth, visibility, Urchins, Turban_Snails, u...
## date  (1): survey_date
## time  (1): hour
## 
## ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
## ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.

Modelling the log urchin to snail ratio

Plotting the EVs against urchin to snail ratio

Building GAMs to test the effects on the Urchin to snail ratio

Model with 1 km recreational boats

total_mod_1km <- gam(urch_sn_ratio ~ s(sst_scale) + 
                   s(norm_openness_scale) +
                   s(mean_rec_boat_counts_1km_scale),
                 #  s(mean_app_fishing_hours_scale),
               data = env_mod_data,
               family = gaussian(link = "identity"),
               method = 'REML',
               select = TRUE)

Building GAMs with averaged points to test the effects on the urchin to snail ratio

The idea of averaging the transects at the same sites is to account for the spatial autocorrelation.

Model with 1km recreational boats and avg transects

total_mod_1km_avg <- gam(urch_sn_ratio_avg ~ s(sst_scale) + 
                   s(norm_openness_scale) +
                   s(mean_rec_boat_counts_1km_scale)+
                   s(mean_app_fishing_hours_scale),
               data = env_mod_data_avg,
               family = gaussian(link = "identity"),
               method = 'REML',
               select = TRUE)

##
